subject: Apex SLO preflight + k6 orchestration for streaming/throughput
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@apex-analytics.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apex-analytics.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + preflight items for the customer-led k6 window

Evan / Sanjay — thanks again for the call today. Short follow-up with the preflight checklist so we can avoid surprises during the customer-run load window. Please confirm items marked ACTION below.

SLO targets we heard today (please confirm):
- Latency p95 target for streaming responses: <= 300ms server-side (Redwood measured)
- Tail latency p99 for token generation: <= 900ms for sequences <= 512 tokens
- Sustained throughput target: 250 rps (non-streaming) with bursts up to 600 rps for 90s windows
- Concurrent streaming sessions: 80 sessions simultaneously with KV cache enabled

Preflight checklist (what we need from Apex):
1) Test accounts: CSV with API keys and role tags (dev/test) — ACTION: please attach.
2) IP allowlist: list of egress IPs for your k6 runners so we can add to the VPC firewall — ACTION: required 24h before window.
3) k6 scenarios: scripts and ramp profile (you mentioned isolated streaming scenario + mixed chat/embeddings). Please include the exact API routes to hit.
4) Test window: please propose 2 windows (preferred PST times) — we will block one.
5) Observability hooks: if you can add a short Prometheus scrape of local client metrics that helps correlate client-side errors.

Attachments I can share from our side: Redwood preflight runbook, sample k6 streaming wrapper, and an allowlist template. I attached a mutual-action-plan to align owners and SLAs for the run.

Next steps:
- Evan to share test accounts + scripts (ACTION)
- Redwood (Markus/Rishi) will provision a temporary test route and add allowlist once we have IPs
- Camila to confirm final window and send Zoom dial-in + war room chat link

If anything above is incorrect, flag it and I'll update.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0172

Attachments: MAP_Apex-Redwood.xlsx (mutual action plan, xlsx)
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@apex-analytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apex-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + preflight items for the customer-led k6 window

Camila — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers inline and attached the k6 bundle.

Confirm SLOs: the latency and throughput numbers match what we discussed. We will validate p95/p99 targets in our early pilot.

Preflight responses:
1) Test accounts: attached apex-test-accounts.csv. Keys are test-only and throttled.
2) IP allowlist: our runners will originate from the following CIDRs: 35.192.0.0/18, 34.120.0.0/16. ACTION: please add to your VPC allowlist.
3) k6 scenarios: attached apex-k6-scripts.tar.gz — includes streaming-wrapper.js (k6 + websocket) and mixed_chat_scenario.js. Ramp profile: 0->250rps over 10m, hold 30m, spike to 600rps for 90s, cool down 10m.
4) Test window: propose Tue 2027-02-24 13:00-16:00 PST (preferred) or Wed 2027-02-25 09:00-12:00 PST as backup. ACTION: confirm which you prefer.
5) Observability: we'll push a small Prometheus exporter with client latency histograms — adding link in the bundle.

We also added a small note about auth: k6 will include an initial token exchange that results in 2x requests at session start (so expect an initial burst).

Let us know when you add the CIDRs and we will do a quick verification ping.

— Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | Apex Analytics
evan.liu@apex-analytics.com

Attachments: apex-k6-scripts.tar.gz, apex-test-accounts.csv
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@apex-analytics.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apex-analytics.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + preflight items for the customer-led k6 window

Thanks Evan — got the bundle and the CIDRs. A couple of clarifying items from the runtime/ops side so we can size the reserved slot for the run and avoid noisy fallback behavior: 

1) Streaming concurrency: you specified 80 concurrent streaming sessions. Are these long-lived (minutes) sessions that will continuously stream tokens, or short-lived (~30s) sessions with 1–2 streaming responses each? Long-lived sessions affect KV cache behavior and memory retention.
2) Mixed workload mix: can you confirm the % of requests that will be streaming vs regular complete-generations vs embeddings? Knowing the split helps us pick a kernel/quantization profile for the dedicated slot.
3) Tokenization: are you passing raw text or pre-tokenized payloads? If raw text, can you provide a typical prompt length distribution (median/90p/99p tokens)?
4) Auth bursts: noted on the token exchange causing double-requests on session start; we'll account for that in the pre-warm choreography.

Operational asks we will complete once CIDRs are added:
- We will provision a temporary route (route id: apex-test-01) and provide an auth test key scoped to the test accounts.
- We'll enable request-level tracing and a temporary 5m metrics retention for the window to capture high-resolution tails.

If you can reply with the streaming session durations and workload split that would be most helpful.

Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Dedicated Solutions | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apex-analytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@apex-analytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 08:56:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + preflight items for the customer-led k6 window

Markus — quick answers below. Happy to hop on a 20m call if helpful.

1) Streaming sessions: long-lived, average ~7 minutes (we stream incremental updates for a live dashboard). Peak sessions hold open ~10 minutes.
2) Mix: expected 55% streaming, 35% non-streaming generation, 10% embeddings/rerank calls.
3) Tokenization: raw text only. Typical prompt length: median 120 tokens, 90p 420 tokens, 99p 810 tokens. We will avoid >1024 for this window.

We'll add a small jitter to session start times to smooth the auth-second-request bursts. If you need per-minute ramp specifics we can provide them.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Engineering Manager | Apex Analytics
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@apex-analytics.com>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@apex-analytics.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Confirmed: Tue 2027-02-24 13:00-16:00 PST test window + final checklist

All — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed answers. Confirming we will run the customer-led k6 window on Tue 2027-02-24 13:00-16:00 PST. Summary of confirmed items and owners: 

- CIDRs added to VPC allowlist: 35.192.0.0/18, 34.120.0.0/16 — ACTION: Redwood infra (complete).
- Route: apex-test-01 created and test auth key sent to addresses in apex-test-accounts.csv — ACTION: Rishi (complete).
- Observability: high-res traces + 5m metrics retention enabled for window — ACTION: Markus (complete).
- k6 bundle received and validated for syntax; noted streaming-wrapper handshake causing initial double-requests — ACTION: Apex to add jitter (in progress).
- MAP owners: see attached MAP_Apex-Redwood.xlsx for point-of-contact.

War-room links and day-of plan:
- Zoom: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/93120348801
- Slack: #apex-redwood-loadtest (we'll create and invite you by EOD Mon)
- Runbook excerpt: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/k6-orchestration-guide (read-only)

Final ask before we go live: please run a small smoke at Tue 12:15 PST — 10 minutes at 5% load so we can validate the allowlist and test keys. If you confirm, I will send the meeting invites and the run checklist.

Thanks team — excited to run this.

Camila
